entities.summary:
Francesco Coppini, an Italian prelate, played a pivotal role in arranging a reconciliation between the houses of Lancaster and York in England during the Wars of the Roses.

Coppini was appointed by Pope Pius II in 1459 to facilitate a peaceful resolution to the conflict, which had ravaged the region since 1455. His efforts culminated in a meeting between the two houses at Coventry in 1459, marking a significant turning point in the conflict.

The success of Coppini's mission had far-reaching consequences, as it paved the way for the eventual unification of the two houses under the leadership of Henry VI. This, in turn, helped to stabilize the region and prevent further conflict, contributing to a period of relative peace in England during the late 15th century.

The legacy of Coppini's work can still be seen today, as the reconciliation he facilitated helped to lay the groundwork for the eventual rise of the Tudor dynasty, which would go on to shape English history for centuries to come.

The 'Reconciliation of York and Lancaster' was a remarkable achievement, given the depth of divisions and violence that had characterized the conflict. Coppini's bravery, diplomacy, and unwavering commitment to his mission make him a fascinating and important figure in the history of the Wars of the Roses.
